annotations.title: Lowest price for a target margin

description: Finds the lowest whole-cent price that keeps a target profit margin after a platform's fees, for a given cost per item. Use it when a US seller asks what to charge on Etsy, Shopify Basic, Payhip, Gumroad, Ko-fi, Notion Marketplace or Square to hit a margin. status is "ok", "not_possible" or "not_practical". With "ok" it returns price_usd, the fee breakdown at that price, profit_usd and the achieved margin. Do not use it for sellers outside the US, for Amazon FBA, for competitor repricing, for VAT, for shipping, or for monthly plan fees (use compare_plans for plan costs). Inputs are platform, cost, and target_margin as a FRACTION of the price (0.30 means 30%). Optional buyer_tax_rate, processor, and on Etsy offsite_ads (none, under_10k or 10k_plus). Default offsite_ads is none, which leaves ads out. Optional cross_border is none, international, currency_conversion or both. Default is none, which leaves those fees out. Rates are dated and sourced, so read assumptions and verify before quoting. US sellers only. Read-only.

buyer_tax_rate.description: Buyer's sales tax as a FRACTION, e.g. 0.07 for 7%. Default 0. Tax is never profit; it only raises card processing on platforms that charge processing on the tax-inclusive total (see each platform's tax_base).

cost.description: Your cost per item sold in USD (materials, labour, packaging you pay). 0 for a digital download with no per-sale cost.

cross_border.description: Optional cross-border and currency-conversion fees, from official pages opened 2026-11-20. "none" (the default) leaves them out, so answers match earlier callers. "international" adds the sourced extra fee on an international card or cross-border receipt (Shopify Payments 1% on a US store, Stripe 1.5%, PayPal 1.50%, Square 1.5%). "currency_conversion" adds the sourced conversion fee (Etsy 2.5% when listing currency differs from the Payment account, Shopify Payments 1.5% for a US store, Stripe 1%, PayPal 3% under a labelled assumption). "both" adds each as its own line. The fee is applied to the item price. Official pages often also count shipping or gift wrap in the base, so add the same rate on those amounts. Currency conversion applies only when the sale currency differs from the payout currency, not merely because the buyer is abroad. Where a platform page states no rate, that line is marked not_modelled and adds nothing. That is not a statement that the fee is $0. compare_plans does not take this field.

offsite_ads.description: Etsy only. Optional Offsite Ads flag. "none" (the default) leaves the fee out, so answers match earlier callers. "under_10k" adds 15% of the item price for a shop that has always made less than $10,000 USD in any consecutive 365-day period. "10k_plus" adds 12% for a shop that has made $10,000 USD or more in any consecutive 365-day period. Etsy charges this fee on the order total, which also includes any shipping and gift wrap the seller charges, so add the same rate on those amounts. The cap is $100 per order, and this tool treats the item as a one-item order. The fee applies only to orders Etsy attributes to an Offsite Ad. Other platforms reject any value except "none".

platform.description: Platform and plan id from list_platforms, e.g. "etsy", "payhip-free", "gumroad-direct", "ko-fi-shop".

price_floor_usd.description: Lowest price to suggest, in USD. Default 1.00 (Marginrule's assumption, not a platform rule). 0 turns the floor off.

processor.description: Card processor for platforms where the seller adds their own (Payhip plans, Ko-fi Shop). "stripe" = 2.9% + $0.30 (default). "paypal" = PayPal Checkout or Guest Checkout, 3.49% + $0.49. Ignored, with a note, for platforms that charge their own processing (Etsy, Shopify, Gumroad, Notion, Square).

processor_fixed_usd.description: Advanced override: your card processor's fixed fee per sale in USD, e.g. 0.30. Replaces the preset's fixed fee.

processor_rate.description: Advanced override: your own card processor percentage as a FRACTION (0.029 = 2.9%). Only for platforms where the seller adds their own processor. Replaces the preset's rate.

region.description: Buyer location relative to a US seller. "us" (default) = domestic. "international" is only modelled with processor "paypal" (adds PayPal's 1.50% international fee, so 4.99% + $0.49); other combinations return an error rather than a guess.

target_margin.description: Target profit margin as a FRACTION of the price: profit / price. 0.30 means 30%. Must be at least 0 and under 1. A value like 30 is rejected as a percent. Margins below 0.0001 are treated as 0. Within 0.01 of the platform's maximum (1 minus its percentage fees) the answer is status "not_practical".
